newsitem.title: ITALY: Milosevic had promised no violence, says Italy.
newsitem.headline: Milosevic had promised no violence, says Italy.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini condemned Tuesday's violence among rival demonstrators in Belgrade, saying President Slobodan Milosevic had promised him his dispute with the opposition would remain peaceful.
Dini went to Belgrade two weeks ago on a mission backed by the international community to try to solve the dispute over the annulment of polls the opposition appeared to have won.
It erupted into violence on Tuesday as pro-government and opposition demonstrators fought running battles in the streets of the Yugoslavian capital.

"The foreign minister, in his recent mission...received precise and repeated assurances that there would not be any violence in dealings between the government and opposition," Dini's office said in a statement.

"We had hoped for the establishment of a round table to set common rules to ensure that elections in 1997 are democratic," it said, adding that dialogue between government and opposition was essential to democratic change in Yugoslavia.
"To that end, we appeal to both sides to avoid any actions that could hinder this (change)," the statement said.

The United States on Tuesday held Milosevic responsible for the violence, after the government had called on its supporters to stage a huge rally in downtown Belgrade, site of the opposition protests.

Independent media said seven people were treated for knife wounds and several police were reported hurt, while a gunman who fired from a group of Milosevic supporters seriously injured a young man in the head.
